agent.summary: The change makes the xs-rs sender behave like xs-c++ at two points on the update path: it flushes a partial DATA block when its worker goes idle, and automatic compression can no longer escalate to zstd level 6 after a transient writer stall. Local update-10pct races were already ahead of xs-c++ and stayed within noise, but the change targets the lab's slow block, where xs-rs sent 5.75 MB instead of 7.54 MB and burned more CPU, consistent with a level-6 feedback stall.
agent.diagnosis: On this controller, congress-sample update-10pct through fakessh and through delayssh at 11 ms RTT puts xs-rs at about 0.67-0.70 s against xs-c++ at about 0.90-0.99 s (2 CPUs pinned), with xs-rs using about 1.0-1.14 s CPU versus xs-c++'s 3.1-3.6 s, so the local gap was not reproducible. The lab's own 61d1dd update samples do show one xs-rs block at 1.833 s versus a 0.959 s block: the slow block moved only 5.75 MB against 7.54 MB, had 8 sender retransmits, and used more sender CPU (1.09 s versus 0.93 s), which is consistent with automatic compression reacting to a stalled writer by selecting level 6 and then keeping the writer slow. Separately, the xs-rs sender never flushed a partial DATA block while a worker was idle, unlike the C++ pool's on_idle, so already-read file data could sit until the 256 KiB threshold or end of transfer.
agent.change: In rs/xs-rs/src/transfer.rs, send_worker now flushes its partial DATA block when it has no queued work, mirroring the C++ pool's on_idle. In rs/xs-rs/src/compression.rs, automatic compression (compression xs-rs chose, not explicit -z) is capped at level 3 so a transient writer stall cannot push it to level 6; explicit -z keeps the C++ adaptive rule. A unit assertion covers the cap.
agent.expected_effect: Removes a tail-latency hold on update transfers without adding frames while work is queued, and prevents the level-6 CPU/rate feedback loop that turned one lab block into an outlier. Normal fast-link behaviour, where the automatic level is already 1, is unchanged.
agent.risks: On a genuinely very slow link automatic compression at level 3 sends slightly more bytes than level 6 would; explicit -z is unaffected. Flushing on idle can add a few DATA frames only when the sender has nothing else to do.

agent.cpp_lesson: xs-c++ already has the on_idle flush this change copies, but it only compresses with -z. Its adaptive zstd machinery in src/compression.cpp and the write-rate observation in src/remote.cpp could enable automatic level 1-3 compression when the writer is slower than ~256 MiB/s, which cut xs-rs's update wire from about 19 MB to 7.5 MB; that would also speed up xs-c++.
